---
title: "How the course works"
---

This is a self-paced course in credit analytics with AI agents. Over four sessions you
rebuild a small-business lending platform — synthetic data, a credit scorecard, and the
decisions built on it — then document it the way a model validator expects. Every session
was taught live and recorded; the recordings are cut into short chapter videos, one idea
each.

## The four sessions

| Session | Theme | What you build or read |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Data and leakage](c1-data-leakage.qmd) | a synthetic lending book you can reason about, and a model that cheats |
| 2 | [The score spine](c2-score-spine.qmd) | a weight-of-evidence scorecard, trained and gated |
| 3 | [Decisions, price and watch](c3-decisions.qmd) | adjudication, pricing, early warning and line increases, and the loan workbench |
| 4 | [Governance](c4-governance.qmd) | the model documentation in this site, written and checked with an agent |

Take them in order: each session consumes what the one before produced. Every video is also
listed in the [video index](../reference/videos.qmd), with each session's highlights and the
full recordings.

## The route, session by session

1. **Once:** [start here](c0-start.qmd) — open a Codespace, run `python verify.py`, choose an
   agent.
2. **Then, for each session:**
   - **Watch** the chapter videos. Each is one idea, a few minutes to a quarter of an hour;
     watch the ones you need.
   - **Read** the pages of the Model Documentation tab the chapter points to. They are what a
     validator would read about the same model.
   - **Run the notebook** in the Codespace, top to bottom.
   - **Do the lab**, by hand or with an agent.
   - **Do the homework** with your agent, and run its self-check:
     `python -m wiki.homework.check <ID>`.
   - **Check** that `python verify.py` still passes. If it does not, your agent changed
     something it should not have; each homework page ends with how to put it back.

| Session | Chapter | Homework |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Data and leakage](c1-data-leakage.qmd) | [H1.1–H1.3](homework-s1.qmd) |
| 2 | [The score spine](c2-score-spine.qmd) | [H2.1–H2.3](homework-s2.qmd) |
| 3 | [Decisions, price and watch](c3-decisions.qmd) | [H3.1–H3.3](homework-s3.qmd) |
| 4 | [Governance](c4-governance.qmd) | [H4.1–H4.3](homework-s4.qmd) |

## Where you work: a Codespace

A GitHub Codespace is a complete development machine in your browser: VS Code, Python and
every pinned dependency, already installed. You do not need to install anything on your
own computer, and nothing you do there can break it. [Start here](c0-start.qmd) opens one.

## How you know you are on track

One command, run from the repository's root, at any moment:

```bash
python verify.py
```

It tells you where you are and whether it works. It never changes anything; it only
checks, and it recomputes every result rather than trusting a stored one. If a check fails,
it prints the command that fixes it.

## Two tabs, one set of pages

The **Course** tab is the path through the sessions. The **Model Documentation** tab is the
same platform written up for a validator, in the order supervisors expect. The course
links into the documentation rather than repeating it, so when a chapter says "see D4" it
means the page a validator would read.
